Existing cryptography-based approaches incur significant overhead, because a cryptography-based mathematical frame needs to be constructed, which prevents deviation from the correct computation. The proposed approach is to reduce the overhead by trusting the computing hardware platform where the computation is outsourced. If one trusts the hardware to do the computation, the hardware can take the place of the cryptographic computing frame, thereby guaranteeing correct computation. The key challenge of this approach is to define what exactly the hardware should guarantee for verifiable computation. For this, we introduce the concept of Correct Execution Environment (CEE), which guarantees instruction correctness and state preservation. We prove that these two requirements are satisfactory conditions for a correct output. By employing a CEE, the verifiable computation scheme can be simplified, and its overhead can be reduced drastically. The presented experimental results demonstrate that the execution time is approximately 1.7 million times faster and the verification time over 50 times faster than a state-of-the-art cryptographic approach.
Author Keywords: Verifiable computation;cryptography;trusted hardware;computer architecture

Title: TransparenKey: TPM-Backed Open-Source Auditable Custody Wallet
Abstract: The cryptocurrency custody industry has suffered repeated failures, from Mt. Gox hacks to FTX insider fraud, that expose the risks inherent in opaque systems. Repeated failures in custody stem from the lack of external observability into system behavior and design, allowing flaws in security architecture or operational processes to persist unnoticed until serious damage occurs. We present TransparenKey, an open-source–oriented custody wallet framework enabling independent verification of key operations. By harnessing TPM 2.0–based Remote Attestation, it generates tamper-evident records for each critical cryptographic action—key generation, transaction signing, and key deletion—allowing end users, auditors, and regulators to confirm system integrity without relying on internal disclosures. TransparenKey replaces institutional trust with publicly verifiable cryptographic evidence, establishing a verifiable and accountable foundation for digital asset custody.
Author Keywords: custody wallet;custody transparency;open source;verifiable operations;remote attestation;TPM 2.0

Title: Scalable, Standards-Driven Tools for Self-Sovereign Identity and Data Protection in Healthcare Clinical Decision Systems*
Authors: E. G. Spanakis; A. Kung; A. Gyrard; D. Jimenez; C. Rabrait; V. Sakkalis
Source title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
Abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare information systems necessitates a robust solution to facilitate secure, efficient, and interoperable data exchange among diverse stakeholders. This paper presents a Standardization Health Care Interoperability Wallet—a digital framework aimed at standardizing and optimizing the management of patient data across varied healthcare platforms. By leveraging internationally accepted standards and advanced cryptographic methods, this interoperability wallet ensures that sensitive health information is securely stored, easily accessible, and seamlessly shareable among providers, payers, and patients. A key feature of the proposed framework is its integration with clinical decision support systems (CDSS). These systems rely heavily on timely and accurate patient data to aid healthcare professionals in making evidence-based decisions. By enabling real-time access to standardized health records, the wallet enhances the ability of CDSS to deliver personalized recommendations, alerts, and risk assessments, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy, treatment planning, and patient safety. Our research examines the architecture of the wallet and its seamless integration with existing Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems and emerging health IT infrastructures. This integration bridges the gap between isolated data silos, demonstrated through a pilot installation and testing phase. We address key challenges in universal healthcare standardization and propose actionable solutions to strengthen data integrity, safeguard patient privacy, and ensure interoperability. A SWOT analysis is also included. Our findings show that a standardized interoperability wallet, coupled with CDSS integration, can significantly reduce administrative burdens, enhance clinical outcomes, and foster a more interconnected, intelligent, and patient-centered healthcare ecosystem.

Title: A Privacy-Preserving Secure Framework for Electric Vehicles in IoT Using Matching Market and Signcryption
Authors: G. Kumar; R. Saha; M. K. Rai; W. J. Buchanan; R. Thomas; G. Geetha; T. Hoon-Kim; J. J. P. C. Rodrigues
Abstract: The present world of vehicle technology is inclined to develop Electric Vehicles (EVs) with various optimized features. These vehicles need frequent charging which takes a longer time to charge up. Therefore, scheduling of vehicles in charging stations is required. Besides, the information of the EVs and its location is also stored by the charging stations and therefore creates a concern of EV privacy. Various researches are going on to solve these problems; however, an efficient privacy-preserving solution is less practiced till date. In this paper, a framework for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging is discussed. The framework uses the concept of Matching Market to identify a charging station and uses the lattice-based cryptography for secure communications. The matching market considers multiple factors to provide the best allocation of charging station and cryptography ensures security and privacy preservation. The use of lattice-based cryptographic hash SWIFFT avoids heavy computation. This usage of matching market and lattice cryptography, more specifically signcryption for EV charging framework are the highlights of the solution and add-ons to the novel features. Overall, the presented framework is efficient in terms of computation and communication cost, satisfaction ratio, slot ratio, charging latency and load balancing index. The performance metrics are compared with recent developments in this field.
